messages.subject: ddply Question
parts:
Hello,

I'd like to reshape some data and am assuming plyr is the right
tool...but can't seem to pass the correct options to the ddply
function to achieve the desired result.

I'd like to have ddply summarize the data in the following way:
For each unique workorder...display the plexity value, and then a
count of the COP objects associated with it (each in their own
columns).

I have tried the following:

plateCount = read.csv(file="http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3734701/
plateCount.csv",header=TRUE)
results = ddply(plateCount, .(workorder,Plexity),
length(unique(plateCount$COP)))

Error in llply(.data = .data, .fun = .fun, ..., .progress
= .progress) :
.fun is not a function.

Any suggestions on what I'm missing here?

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: ddply Question
parts:
> I'd like to reshape some data and am assuming plyr is the right
> tool...but can't seem to pass the correct options to the ddply
> function to achieve the desired result.
>
> I'd like to have ddply summarize the data in the following way:
> For each unique workorder...display the plexity value, and then a
> count of the COP objects associated with it (each in their own
> columns).
>
> I have tried the following:
>
> plateCount = read.csv(file="http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3734701/
> plateCount.csv",header=TRUE)
> results = ddply(plateCount, .(workorder,Plexity),
> length(unique(plateCount$COP)))

You're missing the summarise function:

results = ddply(plateCount, .(workorder,Plexity), summarise,
n = length(unique(COP)))

Hadley
